title: GLASS mocks, tomographic
summary: The 100 mock PTEs of a joint B-mode test are uniform when the analytic covariance describes the scatter of the mocks. It does for Cℓ EB; for Cℓ BB, COSEBIs B, ξ+ B (12–83′), ξ− B (12–83′), ξ± B (12–83′) and ξ± B (2–20′) the mocks scatter 2–7% more than the analytic covariance says (mean χ²/dof 1.02–1.07), so those tests' analytic PTEs read slightly low on the data too. The mocks are matched to the data cell's bins and n(z). The blinded data's Cℓ BB additive-template amplitude, 0.76 ± 0.20, lies 3.3σ above the mock mean, with 0 of 100 mocks higher; we read this as an additive B-mode systematic in the data, which mocks without systematics do not produce.
banner: GLASS mocks under a throwaway blind; the input cosmology is known. The data B modes shown against them are blinded data, which the blind leaves unchanged
lacks: Sampled mocks have unit weights, Gaussian shape noise at the data's per-bin σ_e and n_eff, no PSF leakage and no additive B mode, so this run has no PSF section.
provenance: GLASS sampled mocks on the v2 tomographic footprint (4,582 deg²), 100 of 100 seeds, nside 4096, each bin's n_eff and σ_e from the data
recalibrated DR6 BPZ+SOM four-bin n(z) and bins of CosmoStat/sp_validation#468, the same as the data cell

tables.caption: Each joint B-mode test runs over all ten bin pairs on every mock, against the analytic covariance. A PTE (probability to exceed) is the chance that pure noise gives a χ² at least this large. Mean mock χ²/dof is 1 and the median PTE 0.5 when the analytic covariance describes the mock scatter; about 5.0 mocks per test fall below 0.05 by chance.
Joint B-mode null tests of the blinded data over all ten bin pairs. The rescaled PTE multiplies the analytic covariance by the mocks' mean χ²/dof; the last column counts mocks directly.

columns.label: data PTE, covariance rescaled to the mocks
fraction of 100 mocks with larger χ²

tables.caption: χ² ignores sign; an additive B mode (PSF leakage, a shared shear offset) pushes B modes the same way across scales and pairs. The template amplitude A is the least-squares fit of C_BB = A × 2.6×10⁻¹¹ exp[−(ℓ/2000)²] to Cℓ BB with the analytic covariance; the mean data/σ averages each element over its analytic standard deviation. The mocks have no additive B, so they give each number's null distribution.

figures.caption: Cumulative distribution of the 100 mocks' PTEs for each joint B-mode test, against the uniform distribution (grey diagonal) expected when the analytic covariance is right. A curve above the diagonal means too many low PTEs: the mocks scatter more than the analytic covariance says.
figures.alt: Cumulative distribution of the 100 mocks' PTEs for each joint B-mode test, against the uniform distribution (grey diagonal) expected when the analytic covariance is right. A curve above the diagonal means too many low PTEs: the mocks scatter more than the analytic covariance says.

figures.caption: Variance of the 100 mocks divided by the analytic variance, averaged over each statistic's elements, per bin pair. E rows use ξ± at 12–83′ and Cℓ EE at ℓ 300–1600. With 100 Gaussian mocks a single element's ratio has a 68% range of 0.86–1.14; these averages scatter less.
